newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's opposition UDF reforms into party.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's opposition UDF reforms into party.

text.p: Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces coalition said on Tuesday it would reform as a political party to press for early parliamentary elections and play its part in leading the country out of crisis.
"We need to solve our internal problems and to forget any group or personal interests in order to save Bulgaria," UDF leader Ivan Kostov told a news conference.
UDF deputy leader Petar Stoyanov won a convincing victory over the candidate of the governing Socialists in the second round of presidential elections on November 3.
The result reflected popular discontent with the Socialists' handling of severe economic crisis and the UDF has said it will press for early parliamentary elections.
The UDF was formed as a coalition by 18 anti-communist parties in December 1989. At present, each party has equal voting rights, regardless of size.
Stoyanov was selected as candidate of the UDF and its opposition allies in a U.S.-style primary election in June.

"Unity proved to be the winning strategy for the presidential elections and we think that only united in one party we can propose a national strategy to implement real reforms and end the crisis," Kostov said.
Other party officials doubted whether monarchists, social democrats and other diverse tendencies could work together in one party and said they feared they could lose members.
